item.description: Communications Trainee ChargeUp Europe Brussels, Belgium About ChargeUp Europe ChargeUp Europe is the voice of the electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure industry. EV charging is an innovative, fast-evolving, dynamic sector, at the forefront of the green and digital transition. Our growing membership stands for an EV charging infrastructure roll-out that starts from the consumer needs, makes EV driving convenient across borders, and promotes an open-market model supported by open standards and protocols. Function ChargeUp Europe is looking for a driven, enthusiastic junior professional for the position of Communications Trainee. The trainee will assist the ChargeUp Europe team in all communications activities and projects, including (but not limited to) helping with planning and executing events, supporting the delivery of our communications workplan, and developing content for our social media channels, while servicing members’ needs. This position will offer an opportunity to develop a broad range of communications skills, both through direct experience and by exposure to a network of seasoned communications professionals from the membership. Expected tasks 1. Social media & communications outreach: Creating engaging social media content – both short and long-form – primarily for LinkedIn, ensuring alignment with ChargeUp Europe’s visual identity; Designing clear, meaningful data visualisations and infographics to distil complex information into accessible content; Proactive outreach to stakeholders (e.g. podcast guests and hosts) and support in coordinating activities related to campaigns, podcasts and thematic series; Assisting in drafting written content for social media channels and the ChargeUp Europe website, as well as internal communication tasks and content-creation. 2. Ad-hoc assistance to the Communications Coordinator: Providing administrative and communication support, including document formatting, research, and external communications where needed; Offering ad-hoc assistance in communicating with members and handling day-to-day matters; Collecting, synthesising and analysing information from diverse sources, including data gathering, stakeholder mapping and rapid review of reports to extract key insights. 3. Creative thinking & content development: Contributing fresh, creative ideas to support communications, events and stakeholder engagement; Helping to develop concepts, visuals and messaging for campaigns, events and other formats; Keeping the ChargeUp Europe website up to date; Draft the ChargeUp Europe quarterly newsletter. 4. Logistical support for events: Providing logistical support for online and onsite events (webinars, workshops, presentations), including links, invitations and communication kits. 5. Service to the members: Responding to communications-related requests from ChargeUp Europe members and supporting member-facing activities. Please note that this list is non-exhaustive, and other tasks may be performed under this role. Required skills and competencies Master’s degree in communications or other relevant field; A basic understanding of the European policy landscape and EU institutions; Excellent writing skills in English; Interest in e-mobility; Good interpersonal and organisational skills; Experience in writing for social media, particularly LinkedIn; Experience with Canva. Our offer Targeted start date: asap. Duration: until July 2027. Contract type: CIP (la convention d’immersion professionnelle), full time, based in Brussels (flexible hybrid working regime) Renumeration: per CIP requirements Hiring process Interested candidates should send their application in English by 2 November 2026 COB at the latest to secretariat@chargeupeurope.eu , mentioning “Communications trainee” in the subject line. Please note that interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis: applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible, as the search will be stopped once a suitable candidate has been identified. The application should include: a CV; a cover letter, not written by AI. The cover should not be a repetition of your resume, but a document of maximum 2 pages covering the 4 questions below: What is your motivation for joining ChargeUp Europe; Tell us about a piece of content you made (post, video, newsletter, flyer…) that didn't land the way you hoped. What do you think went wrong, and what would you change? (Include a link or screenshot.); Find an organization similar to ours that does communications better. Show us one example and explain why it works; Pick one of our Linkedln posts from the 4 weeks. What would you keep, and what would you have done differently? a selection of 3 writing examples, preferably across channels/formats; a canva visual you developed. Please note that ChargeUp Europe will not consider applications that are not complete. ChargeUp Europe values diversity and encourages applications from all suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, gender, race, disability, sexual orientation, religion or ethnic background. Only short-listed candidates will be contacted for interviews. Please note that applicants must be authorised to work in the EU. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa at this time. Don't forget to mention EuroBrussels when applying. Share this Job

item.title: Internship - Competition Economics
item.description: Internship - Competition Economics BRG Brussels, Belgium As an intern you will be an integral part of our team in our Brussels and Paris offices. You will be involved in real work that has an impact on clients and businesses. You will be working closely with our experts on a variety of cases in the competition space where you will be able to contribute to the analysis. The work of an intern can be both qualitative and quantitative in nature, and projects range from industry and subject matter research to data collection to the preparation of economic, statistical, and other forms of analysis. Interns should be able to assemble compelling evidence from data and research that underpins our expert opinions. The ideal candidate will have skills in the following areas: You enjoy working in a team. You are passionate about economics. You like conceptual issues and working with data. You want to contribute with your analytical skills and intellectual curiosity. You can propose creative solutions to complex challenges. You have a positive attitude towards new tasks and learning. You are currently completing an advanced university degree (Master’s degree) in Economics or related fields. You have an interest in competition economics and a good knowledge of theoretical and/or empirical microeconomics and industrial organisation. You can draft and communicate effectively in English. A good knowledge of other languages (e.g., German, French, Spanish, Italian, Polish, etc.) is an asset. You can write simple codes in Stata and/or R that are self-explanatory and easy to follow. You have a positive can-do attitude and you are willing to proactively engage with your colleagues. What you will be doing as an intern: Build expertise through training: From the start, you will benefit from a comprehensive onboarding and training program to equip you with the tools needed for a smooth transition into project work. Tackle real-world problems: Use economic theory and industry insights to help solve complex issues faced by our clients. Work with data that matters: Analyse real client datasets using advanced tools and statistical techniques to extract meaningful insights. Develop rigorous economic models: Construct models based on economic theory and industry-specific considerations to provide clear answers to complex questions. Explore current trends and debates: Conduct research into the latest industry developments and academic literature to support client work and stay ahead of emerging issues. Collaborate in a team setting: Work closely with our team to contribute to project success. Take part in the office’s daily life: Join team-building events, sports sessions, and other social activities that enrich your internship experience. item.description: Behavioural Insights Researcher A 2-year Contract BEUC - The European Consumer Organisation Brussels, Belgium € 4.204 - € 4.476 per month gross BEUC-The European Consumer Organisation is seeking a Behavioural Insights Researcher to strengthen the evidence base underpinning its consumer policy, enforcement, and advocacy work. Your role: The successful candidate is expected to contribute to BEUC’s enforcement and advocacy work , especially in the areas related to the implementation of the Digital Markets Act , by bringing behavioural insights - including coordinating data analysis on consumer behaviour and market practices - to BEUC’s work to better understand how consumers’ decision-making processes affect the effectiveness of regulatory interventions. The tasks will include, inter alia: Supporting BEUC's policy and enforcement teams by providing behavioural evidence and analysis in support of advocacy, litigation, complaints, and other regulatory discussions; Analysing consumer behaviour and decision-making in areas such as digital services, e-commerce, sustainability, financial services, and consumer rights; Contributing to the design and implementation of behavioural research projects , including experiments, surveys, field studies, and consumer testing; Translating research findings into clear policy recommendations and practical insights; Managing relationships with external stakeholders (e.g., research institutes, consultants, academic partners); Presenting findings to colleagues, consumer organisations, policymakers, regulators, and other stakeholders; Monitoring developments in behavioural science relevant to consumer policy and market regulation; Contributing to publications, reports, position papers, and presentations. The selected candidate will dedicate 80% of the time to implement these tasks in relation to the Digital Markets Act and 20% to other consumer priorities. Your profile: Master's degree or PhD in behavioural economics, behavioural science, psychology, economics, data science, or a related field; Strong analytical skills and experience conducting behavioural research using quantitative and/or experimental methods; Strong interest in consumer policy , market regulation, and public-interest work; Ability to communicate complex findings clearly to non-specialist audiences; Excellent drafting skills in English (an additional language is an asset); Ability to manage projects independently and work collaboratively in multidisciplinary teams. What we offer: A full-time 2-year contract with a competitive salary package: A gross monthly salary in the indicative range of €4.204 and €4.476 gross , depending on experience; Fringe benefits: Meal vouchers, group insurance, homeworking allowance, public transport, 6 days extra-legal paid leave; Flexitime , homeworking possibility (up to 3 days per week), work-life balance; 20 days/year working from abroad; External consultant contracts are also welcome. A workplace committed to support the growth, skills and well-being of its staff through extensive training and well-being activities; A multidisciplinary and multicultural working environment within an organisation dedicated to promoting consumer interests; A team of experienced consumer advocates who need you to voice efficiently their policy arguments to EU stakeholders; A non-routine job: The opportunity to deliver positive impact in an exciting international organisation with a dynamic, committed and fun team in the heart of Brussels. Location: As our contracts are subject to Belgian law, candidates must be committed to official registration in Belgium and working from our Brussels office. We offer teleworking possibilities from home or abroad, subject to our remote working policy and organisational needs. Hiring process: Applications for the position should be sent by 08 November 2026 by e-mail to apply@beuc.eu with subject line: Behavioural insights researcher . Your application should include the following documents: A curriculum-vitae, with no photo; In a separate file, answers to the following questions: Why would you like to work at BEUC? [ Briefly explain the main reasons that motivate you to work at BEUC, using maximum 250 words. ] Why should BEUC appoint you? [ Tell us why you think we should appoint you, using maximum 250 words .] Describe a behavioural research project you have conducted or participated in and that you consider particularly successful for consumer policies. What was the research question, methodology, and key findings? Any incomplete application will be disregarded; Only short-listed candidates will be contacted; The first round of interviews is expected to take place as of 16 November 2026 with the Manager of Enforcement, Consumer Rights and Competition, the Chief Economist and the Head of Human Resources; A second round of interviews will be planned afterwards with the Director General, the Manager of Enforcement, Consumer Rights and Competition and the Head of Human Resources; Entry into function ideally from December 2026. BEUC is an equal opportunities employer. We encourage candidates of diverse backgrounds to apply. Please do not include a photo in your CV. Project is funded by Stiftung Mercator Privacy notice: In line with BEUC’s privacy policy , the personal data we process during hiring processes is only used for the purposes of carrying out the selection process and is deleted once the process has ended. For shortlisted candidates, we may ask for their consent to keep their information for 6 months after the end of the selection process in case other vacancies that could fit their profile open up. item.description: CEB Internship Programme 2027 CEB - Council of Europe Development Bank Paris, France € 1,800 per month The Council of Europe Development Bank (CEB) offers ten internships in Paris for students in their final year of higher education and recent graduates. From analysing financial risk to assessing social investment, the programme gives you the chance to apply what you’ve studied to the work of a bank with a social mandate. Working with colleagues from different backgrounds, you’ll contribute to assignments in your chosen team and develop skills through research, analysis, drafting or technical work. The CEB finances projects in areas such as education, health and affordable housing, with a focus on vulnerable people. Explore the ten internships Each description outlines the work and the profile sought. The shared eligibility criteria follow the ten roles; role-specific qualifications and skills also apply. Read the full vacancy before applying. 1. Business Process and AI Innovation In the Loans & Social Development Directorate, you’ll explore where AI can make everyday work easier. That starts with understanding how colleagues take a project from an initial idea through appraisal, monitoring and completion. Your work could take you from mapping a process to testing an AI-assisted workflow with approved tools such as Microsoft Copilot. You’ll also prepare guidance, prompt repositories and training materials, learning how to turn an operational need into something colleagues can use. Your profile: Studies in business administration, information systems, business analytics, digital transformation, data science, AI, computer science, engineering, public administration, economics or a related field. You’ll need analytical and drafting skills, knowledge of Microsoft 365 and an interest in AI. Familiarity with process modelling, Copilot or automation tools is an advantage. Full vacancy and application: https://jobs.coebank.org/job/Paris-Intern-Business-process-and-AI-innovation-Stagiaire-processus-m%C3%A9tier-et-de-l%26apos%3Binnovation-IA/1374188955/ . 2. Corporate Responsibility The CEB is preparing its first sustainability report aligned with ISSB standards for publication in 2027. In the Corporate Responsibility & ESG Reporting Unit, you could contribute to that work alongside the ESG Officer and ESG Data Analyst. You’ll help with sustainability disclosures, support engagement with ESG rating agencies and follow progress on aligning internal operations with the Paris Agreement. Tracking reporting developments and writing website and intranet content will give you practical experience of how sustainability information is assembled and explained. Your profile: Studies in sustainability management or related fields such as finance, law, economics or political science. Good drafting skills matter, as do familiarity with sustainability standards and disclosures and working knowledge of ESG ratings and risks. Full vacancy and application: https://jobs.coebank.org/job/Paris-Intern-Corporate-Responsibility-Stagiaire-Responsabilit%C3%A9-d%26apos%3BEntreprise/1374189655/ . 3. Corporate Services Behind the CEB’s lending work are the people and services that keep the Bank running. This role gives you a view across HR, IT, and facilities and travel management, working directly with the Corporate Services Director on shared priorities. You might be bringing together project and budget updates, preparing a briefing or following up on actions agreed by different teams. You’ll also review processes and help explore practical uses of AI and automation. These assignments offer experience in making sense of complex issues and coordinating work across the Directorate. Your profile: Studies in management, business analysis or a related field. The role calls for strong analytical and organisational skills, the ability to structure complex issues and ease working both independently and with different teams. Knowledge of Lean or Agile methods and an interest in practical AI and automation are advantages. Full vacancy and application: https://jobs.coebank.org/job/Paris-Intern-Corporate-Services/1374174355/ . 4. Environmental and Social Sustainability and Climate Change A project’s environmental and social effects matter to a financing decision. In the Environmental and Social Sustainability Unit, you’ll help examine those effects and the climate risks and opportunities that come with them. The work includes screening risks, reviewing borrower information and legislation, and contributing to safeguards assessments. You’ll also support climate assessments covering Paris Agreement alignment and opportunities for adaptation or mitigation. Working through these questions with technical specialists offers a practical introduction to project due diligence and the methods behind it. Your profile: Studies in social studies, political sciences, community development, planning, applied economics, environmental sciences or a related discipline. Strong analysis and clear technical writing are essential, together with teamwork and the ability to manage changing deadlines. Courses on climate risks and resilience are an asset. Full vacancy and application: https://jobs.coebank.org/job/Paris-Intern-Environmental-and-Social-Sustainability-Climate-Change/1374177755/ . 5. Evaluation What did a development project achieve, and what could the next one do better? In the Office of Independent Evaluation, you’ll help gather and examine the evidence behind its findings. Expect to work with project and sector literature, analyse information, contribute to stakeholder interviews and prepare charts for evaluation outputs. You’ll also help with meetings and knowledge-sharing events. These assignments offer practice in research and presenting evidence, while showing you how independent evaluation informs learning and accountability. Your profile: Studies in evaluation, development studies, economics, social or political sciences, urban or environmental studies, business administration and international affairs. You should be interested in social, economic and environmental issues and highly proficient in MS Office, including Excel and PowerPoint. Knowledge of evaluation methods, additional analysis software and relevant professional or voluntary experience are advantages. Full vacancy and application: https://jobs.coebank.org/job/Paris-Intern-Evaluation/1374174555/ . 6. Legal Administrative Issues Staff rules, procurement and institutional privileges all raise legal questions for an international organisation. In the Office of the General Counsel’s Administrative Issues Unit, you’ll see how those questions are handled, working under experienced legal colleagues. You may assist with research on staff rules and disputes, privileges and immunities, or service contracts and procurement. Other assignments can include presentations and knowledge tools, including AI solutions for corporate contract management. It’s an opportunity to apply legal research and drafting to institutional matters with supervision. Your profile: Studies in law, focused on International Administrative Law, Law of International Organisations, or International or European Law. You’ll need accurate legal analysis, advising and drafting skills, the ability to manage deadlines and sound knowledge of IT and electronic document management tools. Full vacancy and application: https://jobs.coebank.org/job/Paris-Intern-Administrative-Issues/1374174855/ . 7. Long Term Investments and Liquidity If you enjoy finding meaning in financial data, this role offers a way to put that interest to work. You’ll be based in the Treasury & Asset and Liability Management Division, collaborating with colleagues in the CEB’s Dealing Room. Historical data analysis, capital markets notes and internal financial reports are all part of the work. You’ll also help develop dashboards covering financial and environmental, social and governance factors. It’s a practical setting for your data and coding skills, with exposure to treasury activities at a development bank. item.title: Junior Policy Analyst - Research and Statistics
item.description: Junior Policy Analyst - Research and Statistics (Temporary) OECD - Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development Paris, France From € 3 240 per month Job Description Main Responsibilities The selected candidate(s) will conduct policy research, data analysis, contribute to the development of policy advice and support knowledge-sharing, including through peer-learning events. They will assist countries with the implementation of education policy; preparing reports and publications; and effectively communicating findings. They will also contribute to the management and delivery of projects and engagement with countries and partner organisations. Analysis and drafting Contribute to the identification and development of policy issues by reviewing, synthesising and interpreting available evidence, and analysing the policy implications. Draft chapters and parts of reports, country reviews, policy briefs, case studies and working papers to present evidence, analysis and policy advice. Data collection and analysis Extract and analyse data and information from national and international datasets (e.g. OECD datasets, labour force surveys, longitudinal surveys, administrative data) and other information (e.g. questionnaires, country policies and practices, and case studies) to undertake statistical and qualitative analysis. Identify and develop appropriate figures, tables and other visualisations to communicate and disseminate findings. Coordination and planning Contribute to the organisation of review missions, peer learning discussions, policy dialogues, webinars, conferences and workshops, in collaboration with countries. Support the coordination of country-specific activities, including managing relations with the concerned country, organising activities and steering the associated analysis. Representation, liaison and dissemination Engage in dissemination activities and developing communication materials such as agendas, presentations and summary notes. Support coordination with partners and experts and ensure professional relationships are maintained internally and externally. Qualifications Ideal Candidate Profile Academic Background An advanced university degree in economics, education, public policy, social sciences, or a similar discipline. Professional Background At least one year of applied research and policy analysis in education or public policy acquired in an international organisation, national administration, higher education or research institution or think tank. Knowledge of education policy issues and education research is desirable. Expertise in one or more of the following areas is an advantage: assessment and certification, digital education and AI, secondary education, higher education, teachers and school leaders, equity and inclusion, basic and foundational skills, curricular reform, policy evaluation and implementation advice and international comparative research. Proven quantitative and qualitative research skills, analytical capacity and drafting skills. Strong statistical skills and/or knowledge of statistical software is desirable (for some of the available positions). Capacity to write well-organised, clear and precise prose in English. Capacity to work with independence and flexibility, identifying priorities, tasks and timelines, and a demonstrated commitment to delivering excellence in work outputs. Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to collaborate effectively within and across teams. An ability to work autonomously and in a multicultural and international environment. Tools Proficiency with the Microsoft Office Package (MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint etc.). Experience with quantitative and/or qualitative analysis data software (e.g., STATA, R, NVivo) would be an asset. An understanding of the potential application and limits of AI tools in a policy research environment. Core Competencies OECD staff are expected to demonstrate behaviours aligned to six core competencies which will be assessed as part of the hiring process: Vision and Strategy (Level 1); Enable People (Level 1); Ethics and Integrity (Level 1); Collaboration and Horizontality (Level 1); Achieve Results (Level 1); Innovate and Embrace Change (Level 1). To learn more about the definitions for each competency for levels 1-3, please refer to OECD Core Competencies. Languages Fluency in one of the two OECD official languages (English and French) and knowledge of the other, with a commitment to reach a good working level. item.description: Senior Adviseur Public Affairs (EU) Provincie Drenthe Brussels, Belgium € 5,118.26 - € 7,233.84 Wat doe je als Senior Adviseur Public Affairs (EU) Als Senior Adviseur Public Affairs EU vertegenwoordig je de belangen van Drenthe en Noord-Nederland in Brussel. Je volgt Europese beleidsontwikkelingen en besluitvorming op de voet en analyseert wat deze betekenen voor onze regio. Je vertaalt ontwikkelingen naar heldere adviezen en concrete acties en adviseert bestuurders en de ambtelijke organisatie over Europese kansen en ontwikkelingen. Ook stel je analyses en position papers op die bijdragen aan een sterke positionering van Drenthe en Noord-Nederland in Europa. Je bouwt en onderhoudt actief relaties met Europese instellingen, de Permanente Vertegenwoordiging, Europarlementariërs en internationale partners. Je werkt samen met andere regio's, provincies en kennisinstellingen en bouwt coalities rond gedeelde belangen. Ook neem je deel aan werkgroepen van het Huis van de Nederlandse Provincies (HNP). Daar draag je bij aan gezamenlijke provinciale standpunten en versterk je de positie van Noord-Nederland binnen Europese netwerken, initiatieven en programma's. Je signaleert Europese kansen en verbindt deze aan de ambities en opgaven van Drenthe en Noord-Nederland. Zo identificeer je relevante EU-calls en financieringsmogelijkheden en vertaal je deze naar concrete mogelijkheden voor de regio. Daarnaast bereid en begeleid je werkbezoeken en evenementen, deel je relevante Europese ontwikkelingen binnen de organisatie en ben je vanuit Brussel een belangrijk aanspreekpunt voor Drenthe en Noord-Nederland. Je standplaats is Brussel, waar je werkt vanuit het Huis van de Nederlandse Provincies. Vanwege de aard van de functie verwachten we dat je in of nabij Brussel woont. Vanuit Brussel werk je nauw samen met je collega's van Bestuur, Public Affairs en Juridische Zaken in Assen, waaronder twee PA-collega's die zich eveneens bezighouden met Europese dossiers. Wie ben je Je bent een strategisch adviseur en verbinder die inhoud, belangen en relaties bij elkaar brengt. Je beweegt gemakkelijk in een politiek-bestuurlijke en internationale omgeving en doorgrondt complexe Europese dossiers snel. Daarbij houd je steeds voor ogen wat ontwikkelingen in Brussel betekenen voor Drenthe en Noord-Nederland. Je weet wanneer je moet adviseren, verbinden of juist positie moet innemen. Je werkt zelfstandig en proactief, ziet kansen en vertaalt deze naar concrete acties. Met jouw overtuigingskracht en gevoel voor verschillende belangen bouw en onderhoud je gemakkelijk relaties op verschillende niveaus. Je neemt eigenaarschap voor je dossiers en zoekt actief de samenwerking met collega's, bestuurders en externe partners. Wat breng je mee Je hebt minimaal 3 jaar relevante werkervaring opgedaan in Brussel, bij een EU-instelling of binnen belangenbehartiging; Je hebt aantoonbare kennis van Europese besluitvorming en van de Nederlandse politiek-bestuurlijke verhoudingen; Je hebt WO-werk- en denkniveau; Je hebt ervaring met stakeholdermanagement en het opbouwen en onderhouden van relevante bestuurlijke en Europese netwerken; Je beheerst het Nederlands en Engels uitstekend, zowel mondeling als schriftelijk; Beheersing van Duits en/of Frans is een pré. Voldoe je niet aan alle punten, maar ben je wél enthousiast over deze functie? We nodigen je van harte uit om toch te solliciteren. In je motivatie lezen we graag waarom juist deze rol bij jou past. item.description: Senior AI and Digital Services Officer (ELA/AD/2026/11) ELA - European Labour Authority Bratislava, Slovakia From € 7,813.55 up to € 8,143.05 per month gross Type of contract: Temporary agent Grade: AD8 Duration of contract: 5 years (renewable) Area: Operational digitalisation Deadline for applications: 27/11/2026, 12:00 (midday, CET) Reserve list valid until: 31 December 2028 The European Labour Authority The European Labour Authority (’the Authority’ or ‘ELA’) is a Union body in the area of cross-border labour mobility. Its aim is to facilitate access for individuals and employers to information on their rights and obligations; support cooperation between EU countries in the cross-border enforcement of relevant Union law, including by facilitating joint inspections; support Member States in tackling undeclared work; and mediate and facilitate a solution in cases of cross-border disputes between national authorities. Further information on the Authority is available on its website: www.ela.europa.eu . The job The Authority is launching a call for applications to establish a reserve list of Temporary Agents for the position of Senior AI and Digital Services Officer. 1. Profile: Reporting to the Head of the Operations Department and/or Head of Sector, the Senior AI and Digital Services Officer will serve as the Department’s lead business-side coordinator for operational digital tools and technology-enabled services, with a particular focus on artificial intelligence applications supporting labour mobility and social security coordination. The jobholder will work across operational Units and Sectors to identify common needs, strengthen coherence among existing tools, translate business requirements into clear priorities, and steer the development and improvement of user-centred digital solutions. As the principal operational counterpart to the Senior Digitalisation Support Officer, the jobholder will connect ELA’s operational mandate, stakeholder needs and service ambitions with the technical expertise, governance and delivery capacity of the ICT and Digitalisation Support function. The role requires a strong understanding of digital technologies, including ICT, data, interoperability, and artificial intelligence, along with the ability to translate operational needs into viable AI use cases and oversee their responsible development, validation, deployment, and continuous improvement. It also requires sound knowledge of EU labour mobility, ELA’s operational activities and the needs of Member States and other stakeholders. Tasks The jobholder will play a central role in shaping a coherent portfolio of trusted, user-centred and interoperable AI-enabled applications that improve access to labour mobility and social security information, support cooperation between competent authorities and enhance the effectiveness of ELA’s operational services. The tasks of the Senior AI and Digital Services Officer will include, inter alia : Coordinating, from the business side, the portfolio of operational digital tools and technology-enabled services across the Operations Department, promoting coherence, complementarity and reuse; Establishing and maintaining an overview of existing and planned operational digital tools, their business purpose, users, ownership, dependencies and development needs; Gathering, analysing and consolidating business needs from operational Units and Sectors, Member States and other relevant stakeholders, and translating them into structured business requirements, prioritised AI and digital use cases, functional specifications, user journeys and measurable expected outcomes; Acting as the principal point of contact in the Operations Department for the CTO and the ICT and Digitalisation Support Sector, ensuring effective business-technical dialogue throughout the lifecycle of digital initiatives; Supporting the prioritisation and portfolio governance of operational digital and AI initiatives, including the assessment of expected added value, feasibility, interoperability, data availability and quality, sustainability, cybersecurity, fundamental-rights implications, operational risks, resource requirements and long-term maintainability; Advising the Head of Department and operational Units on opportunities to improve services and operational processes through appropriate use of digital technologies, data and artificial intelligence; Monitoring relevant digital systems, services and initiatives developed by EU institutions, bodies and agencies, as well as developments in Member States, and identify opportunities for cooperation, interoperability, reuse and avoidance of duplication; Promoting user-centred approaches by facilitating consultation, requirements validation, testing, feedback and adoption among operational users and external stakeholders; Promoting the uptake and effective use of ELA operational digital solutions among Member States and other stakeholders, including by facilitating exchanges, identifying user needs, supporting engagement and encouraging the sharing of good practices; Contributing to ELA’s digital, ICT and AI strategies and planning from the operational business perspective, ensuring alignment with ELA’s mandate, strategic priorities and operational needs; Contributing to ELA’s innovation governance from the operational business perspective, and support the development and coordination of pilots, proofs of concept and other innovation initiatives, including the definition of business objectives, success criteria and lessons learned; Supporting coordination of pilots, proofs of concept and innovation initiatives, including the definition of business objectives, success criteria and lessons learned; Preparing briefings, analyses, roadmaps, decision notes and progress reports for management and relevant governance bodies, and represent the Department in internal and external coordination fora on operational digitalisation; Performing any other related tasks in the interest of the service. Qualifications and experience required 2. Eligibility criteria: By the closing date for applications to this call for applications, candidates must fulfil the requirements below: 2.1. General conditions: Be nationals of a Member State of the European Union or EFTA countries; enjoy their full rights as citizens 1 ; have fulfilled any obligations imposed by national laws concerning military service; meet the appropriate personal and professional requirements for the duties involved; be physically fit to perform their duties 2 . 2.2. Language skills: Candidates must have a thorough knowledge of one official language of the European Union and a satisfactory knowledge 3 (level B2) of another language of the Union 4 . As the predominant working language of ELA is English, candidates must have an excellent command of spoken and written English 5 . 2.3. Education: Candidates must have, at the closing date for applications, a level of education which corresponds to: a level of education which corresponds to completed university studies of at least three (3) years attested by a diploma 6 and appropriate professional experience of at least one (1) year; or a level of education which corresponds to completed university studies of at four (4) years attested by a diploma. Candidates must indicate in their applications the official graduation dates for all the diplomas they have obtained. 2.4. Professional Experience: Candidates must have, at the closing date for applications, professional experience of at least nine (9) years (acquired after the education referred to in Section 2.3 Education). 3. Selection criteria: Essential: At least five years of professional experience in ICT, digital transformation, business analysis, digital product/service management or related fields; Professional experience in driving digital solutions and initiatives involving multiple stakeholders. Advantageous: Professional experience relevant to ELA’s mandate and operational activities; Professional experience with data-driven, AI-enabled or emerging-technology solutions; Professional experience with project, programme or product management methodologies, including agile approaches; Professional experience in an EU institution, body or agency, national public administration, or an organisation working with Member State authorities. Moreover, the following competencies may be assessed during the selection process: Good knowledge of current and emerging digital technologies relevant to public services, including a general understanding of data-driven and AI-enabled solutions and their potential application in an operational context; Excellent drafting, analytical, communication and stakeholder-management skills in English; Prioritising and self-management; Strategic thinking and business acumen; Stakeholder engagement and collaboration. Support visits and meetings involving STG colleagues and campaign partners. Maintain consistent follow-up and provide concise updates on progress, opportunities and recommended next steps.
